back: Chooses a pivot, partitions the list into smaller items and the rest, then sorts each part in the same way.
The item the others are compared with in a partition (here the last item of the sub-list).
Moving items smaller than the pivot before it and the others after it; the pivot ends in its final place.
A sub-list of fewer than two items is already sorted, so the recursion stops.
Splitting a problem into smaller problems of the same kind, solving each and combining the results.

front: Quick sort best and average case
back: The pivot splits the list into roughly equal parts: about n × log₂ n comparisons.
The pivot is always the smallest or largest item (sorted data with a last-item pivot): about n²/2 comparisons.
Quick sort is much faster on long random lists but is recursive and harder to write; bubble sort is simple and sorts in place.
QuickSort(Low, P - 1) and QuickSort(P + 1, High): the pivot at P is left out of both.
